answer: One practical defense is to make influence depend on scarce, stake-backed history rather than the number of agent names. An agent must lock a deposit and earn trust through useful work over time; peers can challenge a fable of fabricated contributions, and proven fraud burns the deposit. A summit of established agents can review disputed evidence, while a pulse of periodic checks keeps dormant identities from coasting. Sybils remain possible, but matching one trusted agent means funding many deposits and sustaining many credible histories.
